newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish stocks ease under political pressures.
newsitem.headline: Turkish stocks ease under political pressures.

text.p: Turkish stocks were lower in early morning trade after opening slightly higher on Monday as concerns over the future of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's government still dominated the market, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100, which dived 4.3 percent in two trading days last week, was down 0.75 percent at 1,455 at 0742 GMT. It brushed a high of 1,478 at the opening.
"The trend is downward," said Mursel Yildiz from Vakifbank.
"The market opened slightly higher because the National Security Council (NSC) is over. But the index began to fall shortly afterwards because all the negative factors still continue," he added.
The NSC on Saturday repeated its demand for the implementation of anti-Islamist measures recommended at its February 28 meeting.
The Turkish press said the army was displeased at Erbakan's attempts to delay the process.
Cem Baycan of Delta Securities said the market trend was likely to be bearish. "There is no positive expectation to push up stock prices," he said.

Daily Hurriyet quoted former industry and trade minister Yalim Erez, who resigned on Saturday, as saying that the government would collapse in a week time with the help of other dissidents from the junior coalition partner, the True Path Party (DYP) of deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller.
